name: Saint Thomas Becket
history: Chancellor and friend of King Henry II, Thomas became Archbishop of Canterbury and defended the freedom of the Church against the king. Four knights murdered him in his own cathedral. Canterbury became one of the great pilgrim shrines of Europe.
meditation: Willing to die for the Church: what would you be willing to give up for her?
life: Thomas was born in Cheapside, London, around 1120, to Norman parents. He entered the household of Theobald, Archbishop of Canterbury, who saw his talent, and in 1155 Henry II made him chancellor. Thomas served the king brilliantly, lived lavishly and became his close friend. In 1162 Henry had him made archbishop, expecting an ally. Instead Thomas resigned the chancellorship, took up a life of prayer and penance, and resisted the king's claim to try clergy in royal courts and control the Church's dealings with Rome. In 1164 he fled to France and spent six years in exile, for a time at the Cistercian abbey of Pontigny. He returned in December 1170. On 29 December four knights, taking angry words of the king as a command, killed him in his cathedral. He was canonised in 1173, and Henry did public penance at his tomb.
prayerTo: Saint Thomas of Canterbury, you turned from the favour of a king to serve the King of kings, and you died for the freedom of the Church. Pray for England and for all who hold authority, that they may govern justly. Give me courage to put God first, even at the cost of friendship or comfort. Amen.
penance: Pray for the Church in England and for those in public life. Give up something today that you hold onto for status or comfort.
